subject: On-prem air-gapped deployment: follow-up & hardware/ops questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hughes <t.hughes@legacybank.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: on-prem air-gapped qualification & next steps

Hi Tom / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on the on-prem / air-gapped deployment requirements: 

Summary from call:
- Primary constraint: fully air-gapped environment (no egress to public internet) for model serving and telemetry.
- Data residency: customer-managed on-prem network, KMS/HSM for keys.
- Ops: limited maintenance windows, change-control approvals, and offline patching model.
- Hardware preference: LegacyBank is evaluating both 8xA100-equivalent racks and a smaller 4x-A40-style cluster depending on throughput requirements.

Immediate asks (we can take these before the next call):
1) Hardware spec: we attached the redwood_onprem_hardware_spec_v2.pdf with recommended CPU, RAM, NVMe, and GPU configs. Can you confirm if your procurement prefers that spec or has constraints?
2) Network diagram: please share a simple network diagram showing air-gap boundary, management jump host, and any existing KMS/HSM appliances (Priya — if you have a diagram, please attach).
3) Offline ops: we need to understand maintenance window cadence and whether you have an on-call rotation for weekend patches.
4) Certificates & KMS: confirm whether you plan to use a customer HSM (Y/N) and which vendor (e.g., Thales, Azure Key Vault HSM, AWS CloudHSM behind an on-prem connector).

Proposed next steps:
- You share the network diagram and current HW procurement constraints (by EOD Thu 4/22).
- We schedule a 30-min technical alignment call with Dev (our on-prem engineer) and your infra lead to walk the spec and offline ops model.
- Redwood will draft a mutual action plan + timeline and expected downtime windows for upgrades.

Attachments: redwood_onprem_hardware_spec_v2.pdf, onprem-checklist.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if it’s easier.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

---
Note: Dev Patel (dev_patel@redwood.com) will join the technical call. Vivek (vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com) is the deal owner for procurement coordination.

From: Tom Hughes <t.hughes@legacybank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@legacybank.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: on-prem air-gapped qualification & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the summary. Attachting a preliminary network diagram (legacybank_network_diagram.png). A few clarifications and answers inline:

- Hardware constraints: procurement prefers to stay under a 6U rack footprint for initial POC. That likely pushes us to a smaller 4x GPU node for the pilot; we may scale to larger racks for GA.
- KMS/HSM: we have a Thales Luna installed in our core datacenter that the security team prefers to use.
- Ops cadence: standard maintenance windows are Tue 02:00–04:00 local and an optional monthly weekend window for larger upgrades. We do not have weekend on-call for infra unless escalated.

Questions from our infra lead:
1) Does Redwood support fully offline (air-gapped) image installs, and how are software/patch bundles delivered?
2) For model updates, can we do an offline model package drop and local-only model registration?

We'll get you a cleaned-up network diagram (with jump host and secure media transfer point) by EOD Thu.

Tom
VP, Infrastructure
LegacyBank
t.hughes@legacybank.com | +1 212-555-0199

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: on-prem air-gapped qualification & next steps

Marissa / Tom — attaching the more detailed diagram and a quick checklist of our offline ops constraints. See legacybank_network_diagram.png (attached).

Answers: 
- Yes, we require air-gapped installs. Software bundles must be signed and we prefer SHA256 checksums for integrity. We can receive patch bundles via encrypted USB at an approved secure media transfer point.
- Model updates: we expect an offline model artifact workflow. We can host models in an internal artifact store; Redwood will need to provide a verification process and a local registration CLI.
- HSM: confirm we will expose signing keys via our Thales Luna; Redwood should support PKCS#11 or a narrow API for attestation.
- Maintenance windows: Tue 02:00–04:00 local preferred. For pilot we can allow a single Saturday window if absolutely necessary (advance notice).

Operational questions for Redwood:
1) Can Redwood provide an offline installer and a documented checklist for the initial install that our security team can review?
2) What are the rollback procedures if a model or runtime update causes degradation?
3) How do you handle telemetry and metrics in an air-gapped deployment (we assume none leaves the network)?

We’d like a short technical runbook that covers install, model onboarding, and emergency rollback before signing off to procurement.

Thanks,
Priya Singh
Director, Infrastructure Security
LegacyBank
priya.singh@legacybank.com

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: on-prem air-gapped qualification & next steps

Thanks Priya / Tom — this is very helpful. Short answers inline and next actions below.

Operational answers:
- Offline installer: yes — Redwood provides a signed offline installer bundle (tar + SHA256 + signature) and a guided install runbook. We'll deliver the bundle via SFTP or encrypted USB per your process.
- Model updates: we support offline model artifact imports. Dev will provide a small CLI tool that performs local verification (checksum + signature) and registers the model into the Redwood local registry.
- KMS/HSM: we support PKCS#11 integration and can work with your Thales Luna. We'll document the key mounting and access controls in the runbook.
- Telemetry: by default, no telemetry leaves the air-gapped network. We support an optional export process (signed and approved) if you choose to allow periodic metric exports through an approved jump host.
- Rollbacks: the runtime supports atomic model swaps with an immediate fallback to the previous model if health checks fail. We'll include rollback examples in the runbook.

Next steps / action items:
1) Marissa: share the detailed runbook + offline installer package (expected ETA: Tue 5/4).
2) LegacyBank: share the sanitized network diagram and confirm whether Thales Luna firmware version is 4.x or 5.x (Priya — please confirm).
3) Schedule 30-min technical call week of 5/10 with Dev and your infra lead. I’ll propose times after we get the diagram.

Attachments to follow: signed installer package + sample runbook PDF.

If that works I’ll open a mutual action plan in the deal record and loop legal for the SOW language around offline support. Vivek, can you own procurement coordination on Redwood side?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
